decision_summary:
The top 10 follows the Borda aggregate of the three judges (quality, practicality, coverage), with one forced swap. Ranks 1 to 9 are Borda ranks 1 to 9: Qwen3.8-27B (29 points), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (27), K2 Horizon MoVA 36B A4B (24), K2 Horizon 7B (20), Gemma 4 26B-A4B (16), Qwen3-Coder-Next (15), Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B (15), Groot-19B-A3B-261023 (5) and gpt-oss-20b (5). Ties are kept in the order the aggregate lists them. Borda rank 10 was Nanbeige4.3-33B (3 points, quality judge only, tied with Gemma 4 12B). That left out the DeepSeek family, which the user requires, so DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B (1 point) takes rank 10. It is labelled chat and reasoning only: it has no tool calling and is not for OpenCode agent mode. Nanbeige moves to honorable mentions as a trial candidate. The other required families are covered: Qwen (1, 2, 6), Gemma (5), Nemotron (7, Bolt now replaces Lightning as the best Nemotron), gpt-oss (9).

Runtime: llama.cpp ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda-b12407 (CUDA 12.8.1) is the primary runtime for all ten. Every llama.cpp command on this laptop needs docker -e GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 placed before the image name (#27330 reproduced on driver 595.99.02); after the image, llama-server parses -e as --escape and refuses to start. Use -np 1 and --jinja. Avoid server-cuda13-b12407 because its NVIDIA_REQUIRE_CUDA is cuda>=13.5 while driver 595.99.02 offers CUDA 13.2, so the container is likely refused (inferred); #28581 is not the reason. --n-cpu-moe N moves the experts of blocks 0 to N-1 to system RAM and counts all blocks, not only MoE layers. vLLM v0.33.0 is a secondary path only: for gpt-oss-20b at 64k (needs --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95, --kv-cache-dtype fp8 and --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN) and for Groot NVFP4 with --language-model-only. None of the four highest-ranked models fits vLLM's 14.65 GiB budget, and vLLM expert offload is undone for Marlin weights (#66264).

The new picks rest on independent Artificial Analysis data (MoVA TB2.1 56.6 / tau3 32.0, K2 7B 44.2 / 27.6) or on vendor data only (Bolt: NVIDIA's own table; Groot: self-reported, anonymous publisher). Every context and speed figure is an estimate from source-backed arithmetic. Nothing has run on this machine. The NVIDIA Container Toolkit with CDI must be installed first, and each pick needs a /v1/models check plus an OpenCode tool-call smoke test before use. I rechecked the load-bearing GGUF sizes live on 2026-11-15 through the HF tree API (MoVA Q4_K_M 21.14, K2 7B Q8_0 8.92 / Q5_K_M 6.39, Bolt 20.51 plus 1.61 GiB mmproj, Groot Q4_K_M 10.86 GiB). I also confirmed the sampling recommendations in the raw README of each new pick.
changes_vs_previous:
Compared with ver/synthesis.json:
- Qwen3.8-27B moved from 2 to 1. Two of three judges put it first on independent AA evidence (TB2.1 79.8 xhigh / 65.2 medium, tau3-Banking 48.0). The practicality judge kept Qwen3.6 first.
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B moved from 1 to 2. Its evidence is unchanged, but the AA review added tau3-Banking 9.3, which is weak next to Qwen3.8 and the K2 models. It is still the 128k pick with the most mature runtime path.
- New at 3: K2 Horizon MoVA 36B A4B (AA TB2.1 56.6, tau3 32.0). New at 4: K2 Horizon 7B (AA TB2.1 44.2, tau3 27.6). Both are llama.cpp only in practice.
- Gemma 4 26B-A4B moved from 3 to 5. Its evidence is unchanged; it was pushed down by the two K2 models.
- Qwen3-Coder-Next moved from 5 to 6.
- New at 7: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B replaces Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (previous 6) as the Nemotron pick. NVIDIA's same-harness TB2.1 for Bolt is 50.98 vs 24.58 for Lightning. Lightning moves to honorable mentions as the fallback if Bolt does not fit in VRAM.
- New at 8: Groot-19B-A3B-261023. It takes the slot that the previous Ornith-1.5-9B (rank 7) held as the fast all-in-VRAM option. Ornith received no votes this round and is excluded; it is vendor-only from an unverified org.
- gpt-oss-20b moved from 4 to 9. Its independent agentic scores are weak (AA TB2.1 13.9, NVIDIA 15.17) next to the new candidates. It stays as the required gpt-oss family member and the pipeline baseline.
- DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B stays at 10 through the same required-family swap. This time it displaces Nanbeige4.3-33B rather than KAT-Coder.
- Dropped from the top 10: Nemotron Lightning (honorable), Ornith-1.5-9B (excluded), Gemma 4 12B (3 points, honorable as the vLLM-native Gemma), GLM-4.7-Flash (2 points, honorable).
- Audit fixes applied:
  - GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 is a docker -e flag placed before the image and is stated for every llama.cpp command.
  - gpt-oss-20b runs primarily on llama.cpp, with vLLM as an option at 64k using util 0.95, FP8 KV and TRITON_ATTN.
  - #28581 is no longer given as the image reason; the reason is cuda>=13.5. A soft IQ-quant sanity note is kept for Coder-Next.
  - --n-cpu-moe is described as counting blocks from 0.
  - The Qwen3.6 smallest vLLM checkpoint is corrected to the 18.75 GiB AutoRound (LM only).
  - DeepSeek is described as the newest DeepSeek that fits, not the only one.
  - Qwen3.8 medium effort now has a mechanism.
  - 65536 is the tested-safe target for Qwen3.8; 88k is an untested estimate.

OpenCode compatibility.reasoningField reasoning_content.
top10.why: Borda 1 with 29 points (quality 1, practicality 2, coverage 1). It has the strongest independent agentic scores of anything that fits. AA TB2.1 is 79.8 (xhigh), 65.2 (medium), 67.4 (low) and 49.1 (non-reasoning), with tau3-Banking 48.0 and Intelligence Index 20.1. Vendor reports TB2.1 73.0 and SWE-bench Pro 61.7. It is dense and fully in VRAM; the decode bound is about 896/13 GB, roughly 65 tok/s, so 40-45 tok/s in practice (inferred).
top10.caveats: AA measured BF16 through the API; the 3-bit quality loss is unmeasured. AA TB 4.0 is only 5.6. The q8_0 KV decode penalty (#27623, from a comment; the >80K cliff in its title was retracted; fix PR #31802 open) may slow decode. If it falls below 15 tok/s, use f16 KV at a shorter context. Output is verbose (AA 86-110k output tokens per task at medium/xhigh). Hybrid prefix-cache misses (#30357) and tool calls leaking into content (#30118) apply.
top10.evidence_level: Independent (Artificial Analysis, BF16 via API) plus vendor. Memory is source-backed; speed is inferred.

top10.runtime: llama.cpp: -e GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 before ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda-b12407, all on GPU. Second path: vLLM vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0 with GrootTeam/Groot-19B-A3B-261023-NVFP4 --language-model-only (10.94 GiB, W4A16 experts on Marlin). Risk: hybrid GDN NVFP4 crash under load (#54331).
top10.est_context: Estimate. llama.cpp: 131072 with f16 KV. KV = 2 x 10 full-attention layers x 2 x 256 x 2 B = 20 KiB/token, 2.50 GiB at 128k, plus 0.06 GiB recurrent state and about 1 GiB compute, giving about 13.9-14.4 GiB. vLLM: pool 14.65 - 10.94 - 1.2 = 2.51 GiB, so about 128.5k tokens with BF16 KV and the 262144 cap with FP8 KV (FP8 KV needs TRITON_ATTN).
top10.tool_calling: Yes. Qwen3-Coder XML, the same as Qwen3.6.
top10.parsers_or_flags: llama.cpp: docker run ... -e GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda-b12407 -hf GrootTeam/Groot-19B-A3B-261023-GGUF:Q4_K_M --no-mmproj --jinja -ngl 99 -c 131072 -fa on -np 1. vLLM: --language-model-only --max-model-len 131072 --max-num-seqs 1 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --reasoning-parser qwen3. Keep --enforce-eager in reserve for #54331.
top10.sampling: Precise coding: temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, presence 0. Thinking general: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, presence 1.5. Non-thinking: temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8, top_k 20, presence 1.5 (README lines 86-88).
top10.why: Borda 8 with 5 points (quality 10, practicality 7). It is the most practical fast option: fully in VRAM at 128k, the same tool format and parsers as Qwen3.6 in both pinned runtimes, and about 2.06 GB read per token, so the decode bound is very high (inferred). One third-party run exists (Blackwall: tools 100, quality index 78.5).
top10.caveats: All agentic scores are self-reported. Some Qwen3.6 baselines were copied from Qwen's card rather than run, and on the vendor's own chart Groot loses to its base on SWE-bench Verified (31.66 vs 36.27). The Blackwall run has no Qwen3.6 comparator. The publisher is anonymous, there is no LICENSE file, and the pruning method and data are undisclosed. Community reports describe altered verbatim path text, which is a direct risk for a coding agent. Run an A/B against Qwen3.6 before relying on it.
top10.evidence_level: Vendor-reported, plus one third-party run without a comparator. Memory is source-backed; speed is inferred.

top10.name: gpt-oss-20b
top10.runtime: Primary: llama.cpp with -e GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 before ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda-b12407, all on GPU, full 128k. Option: vLLM vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0 with the official checkpoint at 64k, Python frontend (the Rust frontend breaks the parser flags, #66989).
top10.checkpoint: llama.cpp: ggml-org/gpt-oss-20b-GGUF MXFP4. vLLM: openai/gpt-oss-20b (native MXFP4, MARLIN on sm_120).
top10.est_context: Estimate. llama.cpp: 131072 with q8_0 KV, about 13.9 GiB VRAM (12 full layers x 2 x 8 x 64 x 2 B = 24 KiB/token f16; SWA window 128). vLLM at 0.92: pool 14.65 - 12.82 - 1.2 = 0.63 GiB, so 27.6k with BF16 KV or 55k with FP8. At 0.95: 1.11 GiB, so 48.5k BF16 or 97k FP8. 65536 therefore needs util 0.95 plus FP8 KV plus TRITON_ATTN.
top10.thinking: Always on. Effort low, medium (default) or high via reasoning_effort; it cannot be turned off.
top10.tool_calling: Yes (Harmony). vLLM supports only tool_choice=auto; llama.cpp enforces calls by grammar.
top10.parsers_or_flags: llama.cpp: docker run ... -e GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda-b12407 -hf ggml-org/gpt-oss-20b-GGUF:MXFP4 -c 131072 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -fa on -np 1 --jinja. vLLM: --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --max-model-len 65536 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser openai --reasoning-parser openai_gptoss --reasoning-effort-map '{"none":"low","minimal":"low","xhigh":"high","max":"high"}'.
top10.why: Borda 9 with 5 points (practicality 9, coverage 8), and the required gpt-oss family member (120b needs 49-52 GiB of RAM). It is the most mature in both pinned runtimes, the only official checkpoint that runs entirely in vLLM, and the fastest (about 205 tok/s tg128 on a desktop RTX 5080, which is a different card), so it is the safe pipeline baseline.
top10.caveats: Agentic strength is weak on independent measures: AA TB2.1 13.9 and NVIDIA SWE-V 52.44 / TB2.1 15.17. Open Harmony bugs: vLLM #65770 and #58825, llama.cpp #30781 (HTTP 500 for array parameters without items; that it hits 20b is inferred). #61239 FlashInfer race (fix not in v0.33.0), so force TRITON_ATTN with FP8 KV. It is the oldest pick.
top10.evidence_level: Independent (NVIDIA same-harness, Artificial Analysis) plus vendor. Speed measured on a desktop card only.

top10.name: DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B (chat and reasoning only, not for OpenCode agent mode)
top10.runtime: llama.cpp: -e GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 before ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda-b12407, all on GPU, or Ollama deepseek-r1:8b. vLLM also works with --reasoning-parser deepseek_r1 (online fp8_per_tensor), without tools.
top10.est_context: Estimate: 65536 with q8_0 KV. KV = 2 x 36 x 8 x 128 x 2 B = 144 KiB/token f16, about 76.5 KiB q8_0, so 4.78 GiB at 64k. 8.11 + 4.78 + 0.8 = 13.7 GiB. f16 KV at 64k (17.9 GiB) does not fit.
top10.thinking: Always on. There is no official off switch; Ollama's think flag is the only toggle.
top10.tool_calling: No. The template never renders tools, vLLM's deepseek_v3 parser raises at init, and AA measured tau2 0%.
top10.parsers_or_flags: docker run ... -e GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda-b12407 -hf unsloth/DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B-GGUF:Q8_0 -c 65536 -ngl 99 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -fa on -np 1 --reasoning-format deepseek. Do not set capabilities.tools in OpenCode.
top10.why: Required-family swap. It replaces Borda rank 10, Nanbeige4.3-33B (3 points), because the DeepSeek family was otherwise missing. It received 1 point (coverage 10). It is the newest DeepSeek checkpoint that runs on 16 GB; the January 2025 R1 distills are older and also lack tool calling, and V4-Flash (159.6 GB) does not fit. Use it for reasoning or Q&A next to an agent model.
top10.caveats: No tool calling, so it is unusable as an OpenCode agent. It is old and superseded by small Qwen3.x models. vLLM '--quantization fp8' is deprecated in v0.33.0 (use fp8_per_tensor). #59738: deepseek_r1 streaming reasoning deltas are not detokenized.

thinking_and_tools: K2 Horizon MoVA 36B A4B (always on; effort high recommended)
K2 Horizon 7B (always on; effort high recommended)
LFM2.5-24B-A2B (always on in the template; excluded)
tools_without_thinking: Every toggle model above with enable_thinking=false (OpenCode #none variant)

new_candidates_assessment.name: K2 Horizon MoVA 36B A4B
new_candidates_assessment.reason: Borda 24 points. Independent AA TB2.1 56.6 and tau3-Banking 32.0 are second only to Qwen3.8 among models that fit. It runs only on llama.cpp (vLLM's smallest build is 20.25 GiB). Use --n-cpu-moe 46, not 44: at 44 the GPU needs 14.95 GiB plus 0.3-0.5 GiB CUDA context. Context is capped at 64-85k, and always-on high-effort reasoning makes turns slow.

new_candidates_assessment.name: K2 Horizon 7B
new_candidates_assessment.reason: Borda 20 points. AA TB2.1 44.2 (level with Qwen3.6 on that benchmark only) and tau3 27.6, at 9B dense fully in VRAM (Q8_0 8.92 GiB + 64k q8_0 KV = 14.5 GiB). Corrections applied: it does not match Qwen3.6 on SciCode, LCR or HLE, and the first vLLM release with support is v0.30.0. The vLLM path is weak (pre-FTPO AWQ, #62743).

new_candidates_assessment.name: Nanbeige4.3-33B
new_candidates_assessment.verdict: Honorable mention (trial only). It was Borda rank 10 and was displaced by the required DeepSeek swap.
new_candidates_assessment.reason: It has the highest independent small-model score (AA Intelligence Index 20.4, TB 4.0 29.8, AutomationBench 53.1). But on 16 GB it only runs as a dense 33B at IQ2_M with q4_0 KV (about 15.5-15.7 of 15.92 GiB), with unmeasured quality loss. b12407 mis-tokenizes its chat prompts even with the bartowski GGUF (refuted mitigation), so it needs --override-kv tokenizer.ggml.add_space_prefix=bool:false (unverified) until PR #31986 ships. It reasons for 158.5k output tokens per AA task. Tool calls route to the Qwen3-Coder handler, untested. vLLM does not fit (smallest 19.34 GiB).

new_candidates_assessment.name: Xing4.0-29B-A4B
new_candidates_assessment.reason: No judge ranked it. All scores are self-reported, and the comparators are mislabelled: Qwen's TB2.0 51.5 is relabelled as TB2.1, and the Qwen3.6 SWE-V is given as 76.0 against Qwen's own 73.4. There is no xing parser in common/parsers at b12407, so tool calls rely on the generic auto-parser (untested). There is a public report of failed write and edit tool calls. The official GGUFs predate the 2026-11-05 mainline merge. vLLM does not fit (FP8 30.89 GiB).

new_candidates_assessment.name: Groot-19B-A3B-261023
new_candidates_assessment.verdict: Top 10, rank 8 (vendor claims only; A/B against Qwen3.6 before relying on it)
new_candidates_assessment.reason: Borda 5 points. It is fully in VRAM at 128k on llama.cpp (Q4_K_M 10.86 GiB, about 13.9 GiB total) and has a vLLM NVFP4 path, using the Qwen3.6 tool format and parsers. Agentic scores are self-reported with copied baselines, and it loses to its base on SWE-V in its own chart. The publisher is anonymous, the repo has no LICENSE file, and community reports describe altered verbatim path text.

new_candidates_assessment.name: LFM2.5-24B-A2B
new_candidates_assessment.reason: No judge ranked it. It fits fully in VRAM at 131k (QAD-Q4_0 12.65 GiB + q8_0 KV, about 14.7 GiB), and a correction shows that vLLM fits via the 12.92 GiB NVFP4A16. But quality is vendor-only: in its own OpenCode table SWE-V is 51.0 against 66.2 for Qwen3.6, AA has no page, and BenchLM gives 34.4 (estimated). #30490 silently loses tool calls as XML text. The LFM Open License bars commercial use by entities with revenue of USD 10M or more.

new_candidates_assessment.name: Ternary Bonsai 2 27B
new_candidates_assessment.reason: No judge ranked it. It is fast and fits at 128k with q8_0 KV (Q2_0 7.10 GiB, about 13.1 GiB total; 196608 q8_0 is not safe). But the only independent quality test regresses against Qwen3.8-27B (12/47 vs 19/47 on the InsiderLLM intent-routing split). Every agentic score is Prism's own, the vendor lists looping and malformed tool calls, and the stock image runs only Q2_0, not PQ2_0.

new_candidates_assessment.name: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B (24GB GGUF)
new_candidates_assessment.verdict: Top 10, rank 7 (replaces Nemotron 3.5 Lightning as the Nemotron pick)
new_candidates_assessment.reason: Borda 15 points. NVIDIA's same-harness TB2.1 is 50.98 against 44.38 for Qwen3.6 and 23.46 for Lightning. The KV cache is tiny, so 128k is cheap. With --n-cpu-moe 50, about 8.2 GiB of experts sit in RAM and the GPU needs about 13.4 GiB (source-backed) plus an assumed 1.4 GiB. Quality is vendor-run only, the machine is below NVIDIA's 32 GB+ floor, and the corrected Mamba state is 162 MiB.

new_candidates_assessment.name: Mellum2.1 12B-A2.5B Thinking
new_candidates_assessment.verdict: Excluded from the top 10; honorable mention as a fast sub-agent
new_candidates_assessment.reason: No judge ranked it. It is a real JetBrains Apache-2.0 release that fits fully at 128k on both runtimes (GGUF Q6_K 10.13 GiB; vLLM AWQ-INT4 7.15 GiB with the hermes / qwen3 parsers). Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q3_K_XL: real VRAM at -c 65536 with q8_0 KV, decode tok/s with q8_0 vs f16 KV (#27623), and an OpenCode tool-call and edit smoke test at reasoning_effort medium.
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M at --n-cpu-moe 21 and 131072: VRAM margin, decode tok/s with experts in DDR5, and how often #30118 tool-call leaks occur in OpenCode.
K2 Horizon MoVA Q4_K_M: whether --n-cpu-moe 46 at 64k q8_0 starts without OOM, real tok/s, and the length of high-effort turns in OpenCode.

Nemotron Bolt at --n-cpu-moe 50: whether 131072 starts or 65536 is needed, CPU-side IQ2_XXS decode speed, and the tool-call path.

The host DDR5 configured speed (dmidecode), because every expert-offload speed estimate depends on it.
